\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The inferential situation}
A scanning process traverses an axis parameterised by $u \in [0,1]$ and at each
step either registers a \emph{hit} or does not, producing a binary record.
Empirically one observes an \emph{excess} of hits in a mid-window near
$u \approx 0.65$. Two mechanisms can produce an excess.

\emph{Pure density}: the hit probability is a function $p(u)$ of position alone
and events are conditionally independent given position; the excess lives in the
rate curve. \emph{Sequence structure}: hits influence their neighbours ---
clustering, excitation, refractoriness --- and the excess is a consequence of
memory.

Distinguishing them decides the modelling programme: estimate $p(u)$, or build
an interacting point process. The instrument of choice is the \emph{lag
profile}, the sample autocorrelation $\hat\rho(k)$ of the hit indicator sequence
at lags $k = 1,\dots,K$. The received reasoning is: pure density implies
$\hat\rho(k)\approx0$ for all $k$; structure implies $\hat\rho(1)$ noticeably
nonzero. A pre-registered protocol declares dependence if $|\hat\rho(k)|$
exceeds a bar (here $0.05$) at some lag with a confidence interval excluding
zero, or if a runs statistic exceeds $|Z| > 3.2905$.

\subsection{What the record showed}
Over $128$ batches containing $9{,}594$ mid-window hits, the measured detrended
profile over lags $1$--$20$ lay in $[-0.0199,\,-0.0023]$: flat, with no
refractory dip at lag $1$ and no excitation bump anywhere. The literal
global-mean reading was quieter, $[-0.0103,\,+0.0046]$. The runs statistic gave
$Z = +0.850$ and $Z = +0.894$ against a $3.29$ bar. A control channel was null;
a synthetic smooth-hump independent surrogate at the fitted rate curve was also
null; and an \emph{injected} lag-$1$ dependence was recovered massively,
$\hat\rho(1) = 0.337$, with the profile argmax at exactly lag $1$.

Two features are not explained by the received reasoning. (i) The profile did
not scatter about $0$ but sat at a uniform $\approx -0.01$ offset across all
twenty lags, with a mirrored $+0.01$ on controls, and $12$ of $20$ bootstrap
intervals excluded zero on the negative side. (ii) The verdict is a null, and a
null is meaningful only if the alternative it excludes is quantified.

\subsection{Contributions}
Section~\ref{sec:density} develops the heterogeneous independent model and proves
the exact null, the curvature bound, the runs bound, the exact variance and the
resulting noise floor. Section~\ref{sec:markov} develops the two-state Markov
alternative and combines it with the former into a separation theorem.
Section~\ref{sec:artefact} proves that the uniform negative offset is a
deterministic identity of the centring operator, and
Section~\ref{sec:diffset} identifies exactly which $0/1$ records realise a
perfectly flat profile. Section~\ref{sec:coincidence} introduces the coincidence
scan, computes its profile in closed form for arbitrary latent rates and settles
its amplitude question, yielding the shape-not-amplitude law and a trichotomy.
Sections~\ref{sec:record}--\ref{sec:conclusion} return to the data and discuss
scope and open problems.

Everything is elementary and self-contained: the product Bernoulli law is a
finite sum over $\{0,1\}^n$, and the Markov $k$-step law is an iterate of an
affine map on $\R$.

\section{The heterogeneous independent model (``pure density'')}\label{sec:density}

\subsection{Definitions}
Fix $n \in \N$ and a \emph{rate curve} $p : \N \to \R$. A configuration is a map
$s : \{0,\dots,n-1\}\to\{0,1\}$; write $X_i(s) = s_i$ for the \emph{hit
indicator} at position $i$, with $X_i \equiv 0$ for $i \ge n$.

\begin{definition}[Configuration weight and expectation]
The weight of a configuration is
\[
  w_p(s) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}\bigl(s_i\,p_i + (1-s_i)(1-p_i)\bigr),
\]
and the expectation of an observable $f$ is $\E_p[f] = \sum_s w_p(s)f(s)$, summed
over all $2^n$ configurations.
\end{definition}

For $0 \le p_i \le 1$ this is the law of independent Bernoulli variables with
position-dependent rates: \emph{pure density} in full generality. No smoothness,
monotonicity or shape assumption is placed on $p$.

\subsection{The transfer identity and the moment calculus}

\begin{lemma}[Transfer identity]\label{lem:transfer}
For any weights $g_i : \{0,1\}\to\R$,
\[
  \sum_{s\in\{0,1\}^n}\ \prod_{i<n} g_i(s_i) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}\bigl(g_i(1)+g_i(0)\bigr).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Rewrite each factor $g_i(1)+g_i(0)$ as a sum over the two-element set $\{0,1\}$
and expand the product of sums; the index set of the expansion is in bijection
with $\{0,1\}^n$, and the bijection matches terms.
\end{proof}

Taking $g_i(1)=p_i$, $g_i(0)=1-p_i$ gives $\sum_s w_p(s) = 1$: the weights form a
probability law.

\begin{proposition}[Moment calculus]\label{prop:moments}
For any finite set $T$ of distinct positions in $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$,
\[
  \E_p\Bigl[\prod_{i\in T} X_i\Bigr] \;=\; \prod_{i\in T} p_i .
\]
In particular $\E_p[X_i] = p_i$ and $\E_p[X_iX_j]=p_ip_j$ for $i\ne j$; the same
factorisation holds for products of three and four distinct indicators.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Multilinearity of independence]\label{thm:multilinear}
For any nonempty set $S$ of distinct positions,
\[
  \E_p\Bigl[\prod_{i\in S}\bigl(X_i-p_i\bigr)\Bigr] \;=\; 0 .
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:transfer} with, on each $i\in S$, the weight
$g_i(b) = (\text{Bernoulli weight at } b)\times(b-p_i)$. Each such factor
contributes $g_i(1)+g_i(0) = p_i(1-p_i)+(1-p_i)(-p_i)=0$, so the whole product
vanishes. Equivalently, expand over subsets of $S$ and use
Proposition~\ref{prop:moments}: every term equals $\pm\prod_{i\in S}p_i$ and the
signed binomial sum vanishes.
\end{proof}

Theorem~\ref{thm:multilinear} is the correct statement of independence for our
purpose: ``correlation zero'' is only the case $|S|=2$, whereas the variance
computation below needs higher-order terms.

\subsection{The exact null of the detrended statistic}

\begin{definition}[Centred pair sum]
For a lag $k\ge1$, window length $m$ with $m+k\le n$, and a \emph{trend}
$c:\N\to\R$,
\[
  A_k^{(c)}(s) \;=\; \sum_{i<m}\bigl(X_i(s)-c_i\bigr)\bigl(X_{i+k}(s)-c_{i+k}\bigr).
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of the centred pair sum]\label{thm:pairsum}
\[
  \E_p\bigl[A_k^{(c)}\bigr] \;=\; \sum_{i<m}\bigl(p_i-c_i\bigr)\bigl(p_{i+k}-c_{i+k}\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Linearity reduces to a single term. Since $k\ge1$ the positions $i$ and $i+k$
are distinct, so $\E_p[X_iX_{i+k}]=p_ip_{i+k}$ by
Proposition~\ref{prop:moments}; expanding the product term by term gives the
claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact null under pure density]\label{thm:exactnull}
Centring at the true rate curve, $c = p$, gives
\[
  \E_p\bigl[A_k^{(p)}\bigr] \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{for every lag } k\ge1 \text{ and every rate curve } p .
\]
\end{theorem}

No smoothness, stationarity or shape assumption is needed: under pure density the
detrended lag statistic is exactly null, at every lag, for every density curve
whatsoever.

\subsection{The curvature confound is second order}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:curvature}
If $|p_i-c|\le\delta$ for all $i<m+k$, then
$\bigl|\sum_{i<m}(p_i-c)(p_{i+k}-c)\bigr| \le m\delta^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Spurious autocorrelation bound]\label{thm:spurious}
Let $v>0$ be a lower bound for the per-position variance used as normaliser.
Under the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:curvature}, for every lag $k\ge1$,
\[
  \left|\frac{\E_p\bigl[A_k^{(c)}\bigr]}{m\,v}\right| \;\le\; \frac{\delta^2}{v}.
\]
\end{theorem}

The bound is uniform in the lag and quadratic in the curvature.

\begin{corollary}[Curvature cannot fake the decision bar]\label{cor:cannotfake}
If the rate curve stays within $\pm 1/20$ of $1/2$, so $\delta = 1/20$ and the
variance floor is $v=(1/2-1/20)(1/2+1/20)=99/400$, then for every lag
\[
  \left|\frac{\E_p\bigl[A_k^{(1/2)}\bigr]}{m\cdot(99/400)}\right|
  \;\le\; \frac{1/400}{99/400}=\frac{1}{99}\approx 0.0101 \;<\; \frac{1}{20}.
\]
\end{corollary}

A $\pm0.05$ hump on a $p\approx1/2$ curve manufactures at most about one percent
of autocorrelation, five times below the pre-registered bar. This is why the
conditioned and literal readings agreed, and why the verdict does not depend on
which reading is privileged.

\subsection{The runs statistic}

\begin{definition}
$R_m(s) = \#\{\,i<m : X_i(s)\ne X_{i+1}(s)\,\}$.
\end{definition}

Since $X_i,X_{i+1}\in\{0,1\}$, the alternation indicator is exactly
$X_i+X_{i+1}-2X_iX_{i+1}$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:runs}
$\displaystyle \E_p[R_m] = \sum_{i<m}\bigl(p_i+p_{i+1}-2p_ip_{i+1}\bigr).$
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Heterogeneity bound for runs]\label{thm:runsbound}
If $|p_i-c|\le\delta$ for all $i<m+1$, then
\[
  \bigl|\E_p[R_m] - m\cdot 2c(1-c)\bigr| \;\le\; m\bigl(2\delta|1-2c| + 2\delta^2\bigr).
\]
\end{theorem}

At $c=1/2$ the first-order term vanishes identically, so heterogeneity perturbs
the expected alternation count only at order $\delta^2$.

\subsection{Exact variance and the noise floor}

Write $V_i = p_i(1-p_i)$ and $D_i = (X_i-p_i)(X_{i+k}-p_{i+k})$, so that
$A_k^{(p)} = \sum_{i<m} D_i$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact second moments]\label{thm:variance}
For $k\ge1$,
\[
  \E_p\bigl[D_i^2\bigr] = V_iV_{i+k},\qquad
  \E_p\bigl[D_iD_j\bigr] = 0 \ \ (i\ne j),
\]
hence
$\Var_p\bigl(A_k^{(p)}\bigr) = \sum_{i<m} V_i V_{i+k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
For the square, use $X_i^2 = X_i$ to reduce
$(X_i-p_i)^2 = (1-2p_i)(X_i-p_i)+V_i$ at both positions, expand, and apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:multilinear} to each surviving product of centred indicators at
distinct positions. For $i\ne j$ the four positions $i,i+k,j,j+k$ admit at most
two coincidences; in every case $D_iD_j$ reduces, again via $X^2=X$, to a linear
combination of products of centred indicators over nonempty sets of distinct
positions, each of expectation $0$. Pairwise uncorrelatedness therefore survives
the overlap $j=i+k$, which is the delicate case.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Chebyshev in the product model]\label{lem:cheb}
For $0\le p_i\le1$, any observable $Z$ and any $t>0$,
$\Prob_p[\,|Z|\ge t\,] \le \E_p[Z^2]/t^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Noise floor of the detrended statistic]\label{thm:noisefloor}
For $0\le p_i\le1$, $k\ge1$, $m\ge1$, $m+k\le n$ and any $t>0$,
\[
  \Prob_p\Bigl[\ \bigl|A_k^{(p)}\bigr| \ge t\,m\ \Bigr] \;\le\; \frac{1}{16\,m\,t^2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$V_i\le 1/4$, so $\Var(A_k^{(p)}) \le m/16$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:variance}; apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:cheb} with threshold $tm$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[At the experiment's sample size]\label{cor:floornum}
With $m = 9594$ and $t = 1/20$,
\[
  \Prob_p\Bigl[\ \bigl|A_k^{(p)}\bigr| \ge \tfrac{1}{20}\cdot 9594\ \Bigr]
  \;\le\; \frac{1}{16\cdot 9594\cdot(1/400)} \;=\; \frac{400}{153504} \;<\; \frac{3}{1000}.
\]
\end{corollary}

The recorded null therefore excludes dependence rather than merely failing to
find it.

\section{The Markov alternative}\label{sec:markov}

\begin{definition}
A stationary two-state chain has parameters $a,b$: from state $0$ the next state
is $1$ with probability $a$; from state $1$ the next state is $0$ with
probability $b$. The one-step operator on the hit-probability coordinate is the
affine map $M(x) = x(1-b)+(1-x)a$; the \emph{persistence} is
$\lambda = 1-a-b$ and the \emph{stationary rate} is $\pi = a/(a+b)$, defined
when $a+b>0$.
\end{definition}

Two identities drive everything: $M(x)-M(y) = \lambda(x-y)$ and $M(\pi)=\pi$,
hence $M^{[k]}(x)-M^{[k]}(y) = \lambda^k(x-y)$ and $M^{[k]}(\pi)=\pi$.

\begin{definition}
Let $q_k = M^{[k]}(1)$, the probability of a hit $k$ steps after a hit. Set
$\Gamma(k) = \pi(q_k-\pi)$ and $\rho_M(k) = \Gamma(k)/\bigl(\pi(1-\pi)\bigr)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Geometric profile]\label{thm:geometric}
For $a+b>0$ and all $k\ge0$, $\Gamma(k) = \pi(1-\pi)\lambda^k$; and if
$\pi(1-\pi)\ne0$ then $\rho_M(k) = \lambda^k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$q_k-\pi = M^{[k]}(1)-M^{[k]}(\pi) = \lambda^k(1-\pi)$; multiply by $\pi$ and
divide by $\pi(1-\pi)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The profile peaks at lag one]\label{thm:peak}
If $|\lambda|\le1$ and $\pi(1-\pi)\ne0$, then $|\rho_M(k)|\le|\rho_M(1)|$ for all
$k\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing criterion]\label{thm:vanish}
Assume $a+b>0$ and $\pi(1-\pi)\ne0$. Then $\rho_M(k)=0$ for all $k\ge1$ if and
only if $\lambda = 0$, i.e.\ iff the chain is memoryless.
\end{theorem}

There is thus no Markov chain with memory that hides from the lag profile:
memory and lag-$1$ correlation are the same quantity, $\lambda$.

\begin{proposition}[Matrix identification]
With $P = \begin{pmatrix}1-a & a\\ b & 1-b\end{pmatrix}$ one has
$(P^k)_{11} = q_k$ and $(P^k)_{10} = 1-q_k$ for all $k$, by induction on $k$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Density/dependence dichotomy]\label{thm:dichotomy}
Fix a lag $k\ge1$, a window $m\ge1$ with $m+k\le n$, a rate curve with
$|p_i-1/2|\le1/20$ for all $i<m+k$, and a chain with $a+b>0$, $\pi(1-\pi)\ne0$
and $|\lambda|\ge1/20$. Then simultaneously
\[
  \left|\frac{\E_p\bigl[A_k^{(1/2)}\bigr]}{m\cdot(99/400)}\right| < \frac{1}{20}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad \bigl|\rho_M(1)\bigr| \ge \frac{1}{20}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
The first inequality is Corollary~\ref{cor:cannotfake}; the second is
Theorem~\ref{thm:geometric} at $k=1$.
\end{proof}

The pre-registered bar $0.05$ therefore separates the two regimes: a
heterogeneous-but-independent scan cannot cross it, whatever its density curve;
a Markov scan with persistence at least $0.05$ must. A measured profile below the
bar excludes the entire Markov family above it. Theorem~\ref{thm:peak} is also
the formal content of the injection control: an injected lag-$1$ dependence must
produce a profile whose maximum magnitude sits at lag $1$, as observed.

\section{The mean-centring artefact is forced by arithmetic}\label{sec:artefact}

No probability is involved here: the statement is about the centring operator
applied to \emph{any} record. Work cyclically, indexing by $\Z_n$.

\begin{definition}
For $x : \Z_n \to \R$ let $\bar x = \frac1n\sum_i x_i$, $r_i = x_i-\bar x$, and
\[
  C(k) = \sum_{i\in\Z_n} r_i\,r_{i+k}, \qquad \rho(k) = \frac{C(k)}{C(0)}
  \quad (C(0)\ne0).
\]
Note $C(0) = \sum_i r_i^2$ and $\sum_i r_i = 0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Total autocovariance vanishes]\label{thm:total}
$\displaystyle \sum_{k\in\Z_n} C(k) = 0.$
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Exchange summation: $\sum_k\sum_i r_ir_{i+k} = \sum_i r_i\sum_k r_{i+k}
= \sum_i r_i \sum_j r_j = \bigl(\sum_i r_i\bigr)^2 = 0$, using that
$k\mapsto i+k$ is a bijection of $\Z_n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
$\displaystyle\sum_{k\ne0} C(k) = -C(0).$
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Mean autocorrelation identity]\label{thm:meanauto}
For every record with $C(0)\ne0$,
\[
  \frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{k\ne0}\rho(k) \;=\; -\frac{1}{n-1}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A flat profile is pinned]\label{thm:flat}
Suppose $n\ge2$, $C(0)\ne0$, and $|\rho(k)-t|\le\varepsilon$ for every $k\ne0$.
Then $\bigl|t + \tfrac1{n-1}\bigr| \le \varepsilon$. In particular, an exactly
constant profile has $t = -1/(n-1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Average the $n-1$ inequalities and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:meanauto} with the
triangle inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
On a window of $n = 101$ positions, a profile flat to within $\varepsilon$ must
have level within $\varepsilon$ of $-1/100 = -0.01$.
\end{corollary}

Mean-centring spends one degree of freedom and the profile pays for it
uniformly. A uniform small negative offset across all lags is therefore not weak
evidence of inhibition but the deterministic signature of the estimator; the
record's ``$12$ of $20$ intervals exclude zero on the negative side'' is exactly
the predicted behaviour, and the mirrored $+0.01$ on controls is the same
identity with the opposite centring shift. Only deviations from the level
$-1/(n-1)$ --- in particular a lag-$1$ spike, Theorem~\ref{thm:geometric} ---
carry dependence information. This also vindicates the pre-registered rule,
which required $|\hat\rho|>0.05$ \emph{and} interval exclusion jointly: interval
exclusion alone is guaranteed for a sufficiently precise measurement of any
record.

\section{Which records realise a perfectly flat profile?}\label{sec:diffset}

\begin{definition}
For $S\subseteq\Z_n$ let $\one_S$ be its indicator record and let the
\emph{difference multiplicity} be $d_S(k) = \#\{a\in S : a+k\in S\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Autocovariance of a $0/1$ record]\label{thm:indic}
For every $k$, $\displaystyle C(\one_S)(k) = d_S(k) - \frac{|S|^2}{n}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$\sum_i \one_S(i) = |S|$ and $\sum_i \one_S(i)\one_S(i+k) = d_S(k)$; substitute
into the raw form $C(k) = \sum_i x_ix_{i+k} - (\sum_i x_i)^2/n$, which is the
expansion of the mean-centred sum.
\end{proof}

At $k=0$ this gives $C(0) = |S| - |S|^2/n$, strictly positive exactly when $S$ is
nonempty and proper. The whole lag profile is the difference multiplicity
function, shifted and scaled.

\begin{theorem}[Flatness iff difference set]\label{thm:flatiff}
Assume $C(0)\ne0$. The profile $\rho(k)$ is constant over the nonzero lags if and
only if $d_S(k)$ is constant there, i.e.\ iff $S$ is a cyclic difference set in
$\Z_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Level of a difference-set profile]\label{thm:dslevel}
If $n\ge2$, $C(0)\ne0$ and $d_S(k) = l$ for every $k\ne0$, then
$\rho(k) = -1/(n-1)$ for every $k\ne0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{example}[Fano difference set]
Take $S = \{0,1,3\}\subseteq\Z_7$, the planar difference set of the Fano plane.
Every nonzero $k$ has $d_S(k)=1$, so the profile is exactly flat at
$\rho(k) = -1/6$.
\end{example}

The ``maximally flat, slightly negative'' shape is thus realised exactly by the
most rigid, most deterministic $0/1$ records that exist. Flatness is a
design-theoretic signature, not a randomness one, and carries no dependence
information in either direction.

\section{A third mechanism: the coincidence (MA-1) scan}\label{sec:coincidence}

\subsection{Definition and exact profile}

\begin{definition}
Let $X$ be the heterogeneous independent scan of Section~\ref{sec:density} with
arbitrary rate curve $p$. The \emph{coincidence scan} is
$Y_i = X_iX_{i+1}$, with marginal rate $\mu_i = p_ip_{i+1}$.
\end{definition}

$Y$ is not independent --- consecutive $Y$'s share the latent cell $X_{i+1}$ ---
yet its dependence has range exactly $1$.

\begin{theorem}[Coincidence autocovariances, arbitrary latent curve]\label{thm:macov}
\[
  \Cov(Y_i,Y_{i+1}) = p_i\,p_{i+1}\,p_{i+2}\,(1-p_{i+1}), \qquad
  \Cov(Y_i,Y_{i+k}) = 0 \ \ (k\ge2),
\]
and $\Var(Y_i) = \mu_i - \mu_i^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$Y_i^2 = Y_i$ since $X_j^2 = X_j$, giving the variance. For lag $1$,
$Y_iY_{i+1} = X_iX_{i+1}^2X_{i+2} = X_iX_{i+1}X_{i+2}$ has expectation
$p_ip_{i+1}p_{i+2}$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:moments}; subtract
$\mu_i\mu_{i+1} = p_ip_{i+1}^2p_{i+2}$ and factor. For $k\ge2$ the four indices
$i,i+1,i+k,i+k+1$ are distinct, so the fourfold factorisation makes the
covariance vanish identically.
\end{proof}

The crucial structural fact is the exact zero from lag $2$ on, \emph{for every
rate curve}: heterogeneity cannot leak into the far lags. Writing
$\rho_Y(k) = \Cov(Y_i,Y_{i+k})/\Var(Y_i)$ for the profile anchored at $i$, we
have $\rho_Y(k) = 0$ for $k\ge2$ always.

\begin{theorem}[Homogeneous spike height]\label{thm:homcap}
At a constant latent rate $q\in(0,1)$, $\rho_Y(1) = q/(1+q) \in (0,\tfrac12)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The coincidence scan is not Markov]\label{thm:notmarkov}
For $q\in(0,1)$ there is no pair $(a,b)$ with $a+b>0$ and $\pi(1-\pi)\ne0$ such
that $\rho_Y(k) = \rho_M(k)$ for all $k\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A Markov profile is $\lambda^k$; matching at $k=2$ forces $\lambda = 0$, hence
$\rho_M(1) = 0$, while $\rho_Y(1) = q/(1+q) > 0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Trichotomy of profile shapes]\label{thm:trichotomy}
The three mechanisms are pairwise separated by the first two lags alone:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
mechanism & lag $1$ & lag $2$ & shape\\
\midrule
pure density & $0$ & $0$ & flat\\
Markov, $\lambda\ne0$ & $\lambda\ne0$ & $\lambda^2\ne0$ & geometric\\
coincidence & $>0$ & $0$ & one spike\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The amplitude question, settled}

Theorem~\ref{thm:homcap} invites the inference that a spike above $1/2$ rules the
coincidence mechanism out. That inference is wrong, and the reason is a
cancellation.

\begin{theorem}[Closed form of the spike height]\label{thm:closedform}
Write $a = p_i$, $b = p_{i+1}$, $c = p_{i+2}$ with $a,b\in(0,1)$. Then
\[
  \rho_Y(1) \;=\; \frac{c\,(1-b)}{1-a\,b}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Divide $abc(1-b)$ by $ab-(ab)^2 = ab(1-ab)$; the factor $ab$ cancels.
\end{proof}

The spike height therefore does not depend on the coincidence scan's own
marginal rate $\mu_i = ab$ at all, only on the three latent rates.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:ltone}
For $a,b\in(0,1)$ and $c\le1$ we have $\rho_Y(1)<1$; and for $c\ge0$,
$\rho_Y(1)\ge0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
$1-ab>0$, so $\rho_Y(1)<1$ reduces to $c(1-b)<1-ab$, which holds because
$c(1-b)\le 1-b \le 1-ab$ with strictness from $b(1-a)>0$. Nonnegativity is
immediate.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp bound over a rate window]\label{thm:spikebound}
Suppose all three latent rates lie in $[l,u]$ with $0<l\le u<1$. Then
\[
  \rho_Y(1) \;\le\; \Sigma(l,u) \;:=\; \frac{u(1-l)}{1-ul}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Clearing denominators, the claim is $c(1-b)(1-ul)\le u(1-l)(1-ab)$. Use $c\le u$
and then the exact identity
\[
  u(1-l)(1-ab) - u(1-b)(1-ul) \;=\; u\bigl[(b-l)(1-u) + (u-a)(1-l)\,b\bigr],
\]
whose right side is a sum of products of nonnegative quantities under the window
hypotheses. In words: the height increases in $a$ and $c$ and decreases in $b$,
so the extremum sits at $a=c=u$, $b=l$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The bound is attained]\label{thm:attained}
Let $\mathrm{alt}_{l,u}$ be the alternating rate curve taking value $l$ at odd
positions and $u$ at even ones. For $0<l\le u<1$ the coincidence scan over
$\mathrm{alt}_{l,u}$ has, anchored at position $0$,
$\rho_Y(1) = \Sigma(l,u) = u(1-l)/(1-ul)$.
\end{theorem}

Hence $\Sigma(l,u)$ is the maximum, not merely an upper bound.

\begin{theorem}[Heterogeneity breaks the homogeneous cap]\label{thm:beatcap}
With rates ranging over $[1/10,9/10]$ the alternating curve achieves
\[
  \rho_Y(1) = \frac{(9/10)(9/10)}{1-9/100} = \frac{81}{91} \approx 0.890 \;>\; \tfrac12,
\]
while at any constant rate $q\in(0,1)$ the spike is $q/(1+q) < 1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The supremum is exactly one]\label{thm:supone}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a latent rate curve with all values in $(0,1)$
whose coincidence spike satisfies $1-\varepsilon < \rho_Y(1) < 1$. Hence
$\sup\rho_Y(1) = 1$ over all such curves, and the supremum is not attained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Take $\mathrm{alt}_{t,1-t}$ for small $t>0$: then
$\rho_Y(1) = (1-t)^2/\bigl(1-t(1-t)\bigr) \to 1$ as $t\downarrow0$ (explicitly,
$t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $t\le1/4$ suffice). Non-attainment is
Theorem~\ref{thm:ltone}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The shape-not-amplitude law}

\begin{theorem}[Amplitude carries no mechanism information]\label{thm:shapelaw}
For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a latent rate curve whose coincidence scan has
\[
  \rho_Y(1) > 1-\varepsilon \qquad\text{and}\qquad \rho_Y(k) = 0 \ \text{ for all } k\ge2 .
\]
\end{theorem}

Every height in $(0,1)$ is realisable as a coincidence spike, while the exact
zeros beyond lag $1$ persist regardless. Two methodological corollaries follow.

\begin{enumerate}
\item No amplitude threshold can ever exclude the coincidence mechanism; a
``spike too tall to be a coincidence effect'' does not exist.
\item A flat, slightly negative measured profile excludes the coincidence
mechanism at every amplitude simultaneously --- a strictly stronger exclusion
than any height comparison, because it uses the shape invariant (zeros from lag
$2$) rather than the amplitude.
\end{enumerate}

The cap $q/(1+q)<1/2$ was therefore a homogeneity artefact: a true statement
about constant-rate latent scans and a false guide to heterogeneous ones ---
exactly the class the investigation could not assume away, since positional
heterogeneity is the phenomenon under study.

\section{Reading the experimental record}\label{sec:record}

\begin{center}
\renewcommand{\arraystretch}{1.25}
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{0.42\textwidth}p{0.52\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
observation & exact account\\
\midrule
detrended $\hat\rho(k)\in[-0.0199,-0.0023]$, lags $1$--$20$ &
population value exactly $0$ (Thm.~\ref{thm:exactnull}); scatter inside the
$1/(16mt^2)$ noise floor (Thm.~\ref{thm:noisefloor})\\
uniform $\approx-0.01$ offset; $12/20$ intervals exclude zero, negative side &
forced by centring: mean profile level is $-1/(n-1)$
(Thms.~\ref{thm:meanauto},~\ref{thm:flat})\\
mirrored $+0.01$ on controls &
same identity with the opposite centring shift; an opposite-sign
shared-magnitude artefact, not structure\\
literal reading $[-0.0103,+0.0046]$ agrees with conditioned reading &
curvature confound bounded by $\delta^2/v \approx 0.0101$ uniformly in the lag
(Thm.~\ref{thm:spurious}, Cor.~\ref{cor:cannotfake})\\
synthetic smooth-hump surrogate also null &
Thm.~\ref{thm:spurious} again: a hump cannot manufacture more than $\approx1\%$\\
runs $Z = +0.850/+0.894$ vs bar $3.29$ &
heterogeneity perturbs expected alternations only at order $\delta^2$ near
$c=1/2$ (Thm.~\ref{thm:runsbound})\\
injected lag-$1$ dependence detected, $\hat\rho(1)=0.337$, argmax at lag $1$ &
Markov profile is $\lambda^k$, peaking at lag $1$
(Thms.~\ref{thm:geometric},~\ref{thm:peak})\\
verdict: no sequence structure &
below-bar reading excludes every Markov chain with $|\lambda|\ge0.05$
(Thm.~\ref{thm:dichotomy}); flat shape excludes coincidence at all amplitudes
(Thm.~\ref{thm:shapelaw})\\
flatness itself &
not informative: attained by cyclic difference sets
(Thms.~\ref{thm:flatiff},~\ref{thm:dslevel})\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Terminal characterisation.} Given position, neighbouring hits
carry no information about each other. The mid-window excess near
$u \approx 0.65$ is pure density --- rate heterogeneity along the scan axis ---
and not sequence structure of any of the three kinds analysed.

\medskip
\noindent\textbf{Operational law.} Future predictive gains come from modelling
the positional density curve $p(u)$ itself, never from Markov, neighbourhood or
clustering structure on the hit sequence.

\section{Algorithms}

\textbf{(A) Detrended lag profile.} Given a binary record and an estimated rate
curve $\hat p$, compute
$\hat\rho(k) = \bigl(\sum_{i<m}(x_i-\hat p_i)(x_{i+k}-\hat p_{i+k})\bigr)/
\bigl(\sum_{i<m}\hat p_i(1-\hat p_i)\bigr)$ for $k=1,\dots,K$; cost $O(Km)$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:exactnull} gives its population value, Theorem~\ref{thm:variance}
its exact variance, Theorem~\ref{thm:noisefloor} its threshold.

\smallskip
\textbf{(B) Artefact level check.} Compute the mean of the measured profile over
the $n-1$ nonzero lags and compare with $-1/(n-1)$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:meanauto}); cost $O(n)$. This must precede any interpretation
of a uniform offset.

\smallskip
\textbf{(C) Shape classifier.} From $(\hat\rho(1),\hat\rho(2))$: both
$\approx 0$ gives density; $\hat\rho(2)\approx\hat\rho(1)^2\ne0$ gives Markov
with $\lambda = \hat\rho(1)$; $\hat\rho(1)\ne0$ with $\hat\rho(2)\approx0$ gives
coincidence. Cost $O(1)$; justified by Theorem~\ref{thm:trichotomy}.

\smallskip
\textbf{(D) Extremal spike search.} Given a rate window $[l,u]$, the maximum
achievable coincidence spike is $\Sigma(l,u) = u(1-l)/(1-ul)$, attained by the
alternating curve (Theorems~\ref{thm:spikebound},~\ref{thm:attained}); cost
$O(1)$, no optimisation loop required.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{What went wrong with the naive picture}
The conjecture ``under pure density the measured autocorrelation is zero'' is
false twice over, and the failures differ in character. Curvature in the rate
curve produces a genuine nonzero expectation $\sum_i(p_i-c)(p_{i+k}-c)$ --- a
real bias, but second order (Theorem~\ref{thm:spurious}). The level $-1/(n-1)$,
by contrast, is not statistical bias but an algebraic identity of the estimator
(Theorem~\ref{thm:meanauto}) holding for every record, random or not. Both are
``needs a different definition'' failures: the correct null value is $-1/(n-1)$,
not $0$, and the correct statement of independence is the multilinear identity
of Theorem~\ref{thm:multilinear}, not vanishing correlation.

\subsection{Why this is an exclusion, not a shrug}
Three ingredients turn a flat profile into a positive claim: an exact population
null for the honest statistic (Theorem~\ref{thm:exactnull}); a quantified
alternative whose signature exceeds the bar (Theorem~\ref{thm:dichotomy}); and a
noise floor showing the null cannot arise by accident at the given sample size
(Theorem~\ref{thm:noisefloor}, Corollary~\ref{cor:floornum}). Absent the latter
two, a flat profile would be an absence of evidence; with them it is evidence of
absence for a precisely delimited family of alternatives.

\subsection{Shape versus amplitude}
Section~\ref{sec:coincidence} isolates a principle worth stating on its own. In a
mechanism family parameterised by a nuisance curve, the amplitude of a summary
statistic can range over an entire interval while a structural invariant of that
statistic --- here exact vanishing from lag $2$ --- is preserved throughout. The
invariant identifies; the amplitude does not. Amplitude-threshold exclusions are
therefore systematically weaker, and sometimes invalid, compared with shape-based
tests.

\subsection{Scope}
The analysis is model-theoretic and unconditional. Its application to the
experimental record inherits that record's scope: the excess was established on
one seed lineage, and provenance rests on a disclosed checksum of the positional
data. A pooled multi-seed amplitude test remains outstanding; the machinery here
transfers unchanged if an excess is re-established elsewhere, since none of the
theorems reference the particular record.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{Beyond MA-1.} The coincidence rule $Y_i = X_iX_{i+1}$ is the shortest
moving-average mechanism. The natural next object is $Y_i = \prod_{j<w}X_{i+j}$,
whose profile should be a $(w-1)$-step staircase with exact zeros beyond; the
amplitude analysis should generalise to a window bound in $w$ variables.
\item \emph{Higher-order shape invariants.} Two lags separate three mechanisms;
mechanisms with equal second-order profiles (e.g.\ hidden-Markov emissions) will
require third-order statistics, for which Theorem~\ref{thm:multilinear} is
already the right tool under the density null.
\item \emph{Estimation of the density curve.} The operational law says to model
$p(u)$. Theorem~\ref{thm:variance} gives the variance budget; open is a minimax
rate for $p$ under smoothness assumptions, and how the noise floor degrades when
$\hat p$ replaces $p$.
\item \emph{Sharpening the exclusion.} Chebyshev is lossy; a Bernstein-type bound
tailored to the bounded increments of $A_k^{(p)}$ would replace $1/(16mt^2)$ by
an exponential bound, tightening the excluded parameter range.
\item \emph{The difference-set boundary.} Theorem~\ref{thm:flatiff} characterises
exact flatness by cyclic difference sets. The quantitative version --- how close
$d_S$ must be to constant for $\varepsilon$-flatness, and the measure of such
$S$ --- connects the artefact analysis to design theory.
\item \emph{Scale and locality.} Outstanding on the broader programme:
deviations from scale-smoothness at larger window scales, factor-local structure
beyond scan order, effectivity of the MA-1 reading, and a pooled multi-seed
amplitude confirmation.
\end{itemize}

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

A flat lag profile is one of the most common empirical findings in the analysis
of event sequences, and one of the most commonly over- and under-interpreted.
Under pure density the honestly detrended statistic has population value exactly
zero at every lag for every rate curve; the literal reading is off by at most
$\delta^2/v$; the statistic's exact variance yields a noise floor; and a
two-state Markov alternative with persistence at least the decision bar must be
detected. Hence a flat profile is a genuine exclusion of sequence structure. At
the same time the small uniform negative offset that accompanies flat profiles is
no signal at all: the average autocorrelation over the nonzero lags of any
mean-centred record is exactly $-1/(n-1)$, and among $0/1$ records exact flatness
at that level characterises cyclic difference sets. Finally, the coincidence scan
is separated from the other two mechanisms by the first two lags, and its spike
amplitude is an unbounded parameter with supremum exactly $1$, so amplitude can
never identify it while shape always can.

Given position, neighbouring hits carry no information about each other. The
excess is density, and the modelling effort belongs on the density curve.

\end{document}

"""
Density versus Dependence in a Binary Scan
==========================================

Numerical demonstrations of the exact results on hit-indicator lag profiles.

The programme:

  1. The mean-centring identity.  For ANY cyclic record of length n, the average
     sample autocorrelation over the n-1 nonzero lags is exactly -1/(n-1).

  2. Difference sets realise the flat profile.  For a 0/1 record with support S,
     C(k) = d_S(k) - |S|^2/n; flat over nonzero lags iff S is a cyclic
     difference set, and the level is then exactly -1/(n-1).

  3. Pure density is exactly null when detrended at the true rate curve, and the
     literal global-mean reading is bounded by delta^2 / v uniformly in the lag.

  4. The Markov alternative has profile exactly lambda^k, peaking at lag 1.

  5. The coincidence (MA-1) scan has covariance p_i p_{i+1} p_{i+2} (1-p_{i+1})
     at lag 1 and EXACTLY zero at every lag >= 2, for every rate curve; its
     lag-1 correlation is c(1-b)/(1-ab), maximised over [l,u] by
     u(1-l)/(1-u l), attained by the alternating curve, with supremum 1.

  6. The noise floor 1/(16 m t^2), and the three-way shape classifier.

Self-contained: standard library plus (optional) numpy is NOT required.
Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 0.  Elementary helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cyclic_autocov(x: Sequence[float], k: int) -> float:
    """Mean-centred cyclic autocovariance C(k) = sum_i r_i r_{i+k}, r = x - mean."""
    n = len(x)
    mean = sum(x) / n
    r = [xi - mean for xi in x]
    return sum(r[i] * r[(i + k) % n] for i in range(n))


def cyclic_autocorr_profile(x: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """rho(k) = C(k)/C(0) for k = 1 .. n-1."""
    n = len(x)
    c0 = cyclic_autocov(x, 0)
    if c0 == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("constant record: autocorrelation undefined")
    return [cyclic_autocov(x, k) / c0 for k in range(1, n)]


def difference_multiplicity(support: Sequence[int], n: int, k: int) -> int:
    """d_S(k) = #{a in S : a + k mod n in S}."""
    s = set(a % n for a in support)
    return sum(1 for a in s if (a + k) % n in s)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 3.  Pure density: exact null, and the second-order curvature bound
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def exact_bernoulli_expectation(p: Sequence[float],
                                f: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], float]) -> float:
    """Exact expectation over all 2^n configurations of a product-Bernoulli law."""
    n = len(p)
    total = 0.0
    for s in product((0, 1), repeat=n):
        w = 1.0
        for i in range(n):
            w *= p[i] if s[i] else 1.0 - p[i]
        total += w * f(s)
    return total


def centered_pair_sum(s: Tuple[int, ...], k: int, m: int,
                      c: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return sum((s[i] - c[i]) * (s[i + k] - c[i + k]) for i in range(m))

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 5.  The Markov alternative: profile exactly lambda^k
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def markov_profile(a: float, b: float, kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    """rho(k) computed by iterating the affine one-step map, not by the formula."""
    lam = 1.0 - a - b
    pi = a / (a + b)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        x = 1.0
        for _ in range(k):
            x = x * (1 - b) + (1 - x) * a
        cov = pi * (x - pi)
        out.append(cov / (pi * (1 - pi)))
    return out

        print(f"\n  a = {a}, b = {b}   lambda = {lam:+.3f}   "
              f"stationary rate = {a/(a+b):.4f}")
        print(f"    iterated profile : {[round(v, 8) for v in prof]}")
        print(f"    lambda^k         : {[round(v, 8) for v in pred]}")
        print(f"    max deviation    : {err:.2e}     argmax lag = {argmax}")
    print()

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 6.  The coincidence (MA-1) scan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ma_profile_exact(p: Sequence[float], i: int, kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    """Lag profile of Y_j = X_j X_{j+1} anchored at i, by exact enumeration."""
    n = len(p)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        if i + k + 1 >= n:
            break
        mu_i = p[i] * p[i + 1]
        mu_ik = p[i + k] * p[i + k + 1]
        cov = exact_bernoulli_expectation(
            p, lambda s, i=i, k=k, mu_i=mu_i, mu_ik=mu_ik:
            (s[i] * s[i + 1] - mu_i) * (s[i + k] * s[i + k + 1] - mu_ik))
        var = mu_i - mu_i ** 2
        out.append(cov / var)
    return out


def spike_bound(l: float, u: float) -> float:
    """Sigma(l,u) = u(1-l)/(1-ul): the sharp maximum coincidence spike."""
    return u * (1 - l) / (1 - u * l)


def alt_rate(l: float, u: float, n: int) -> List[float]:
    """The alternating rate curve u, l, u, l, ... which attains the bound."""
    return [l if j % 2 == 1 else u for j in range(n)]

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 7.  The three-way shape classifier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def classify_profile(rho1: float, rho2: float, tol: float = 0.01) -> str:
    """Classify a mechanism from the first two lags alone (Trichotomy theorem)."""
    if abs(rho1) <= tol and abs(rho2) <= tol:
        return "pure density (flat)"
    if abs(rho1) > tol and abs(rho2) <= tol:
        return "coincidence / MA-1 (one spike)"
    if abs(rho2 - rho1 ** 2) <= tol:
        return f"Markov (geometric, lambda ~ {rho1:+.3f})"
    return "unclassified"

        samples.append((f"Markov a={a}, b={b}", prof[0], prof[1]))

    # coincidence scans
    for name, p in [("coincidence, q = 0.6", [0.6] * n),
                    ("coincidence, alternating 0.1/0.9", alt_rate(0.1, 0.9, n))]:
        prof = ma_profile_exact(p, 0, 2)
        samples.append((name, prof[0], prof[1]))

    # the measured record
    samples.append(("MEASURED RECORD (lags 1,2)", -0.0199, -0.0104))

    print(f"  {'mechanism':<36}{'rho(1)':>10}{'rho(2)':>10}   verdict")

    for name, r1, r2 in samples:

    print()
    print("  Note the measured record: both lags sit at the arithmetic artefact")
    print("  level, far below the 0.05 bar.  Density, and nothing else.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 8.  A Monte-Carlo replay of the experimental verdict
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def simulate_scan_density(rate: Callable[[float], float], n: int,
                          rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    return [1 if rng.random() < rate(i / (n - 1)) else 0 for i in range(n)]


def simulate_scan_markov(a: float, b: float, n: int,
                         rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    pi = a / (a + b)
    x = 1 if rng.random() < pi else 0
    out = [x]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        x = (1 if rng.random() >= b else 0) if x == 1 else (1 if rng.random() < a else 0)
        out.append(x)
    return out


def detrended_profile(x: Sequence[int], p_hat: Sequence[float],
                      kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    n = len(x)
    denom = sum(ph * (1 - ph) for ph in p_hat)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        m = n - k
        num = sum((x[i] - p_hat[i]) * (x[i + k] - p_hat[i + k]) for i in range(m))
        scale = sum(p_hat[i] * (1 - p_hat[i]) for i in range(m))
        out.append(num / scale if scale else 0.0)
    return out


def demo_monte_carlo_replay(seed: int = 599) -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8.  MONTE-CARLO REPLAY:  DENSITY IS NULL, INJECTED DEPENDENCE IS CAUGHT")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = 9594

    # (a) pure density with a mid-window hump at u ~ 0.65
    def rate(u: float) -> float:
        return 0.50 + 0.05 * math.exp(-((u - 0.65) ** 2) / (2 * 0.08 ** 2))

    x = simulate_scan_density(rate, n, rng)
    p_hat = [rate(i / (n - 1)) for i in range(n)]
    prof = detrended_profile(x, p_hat, 20)
    print(f"\n  (a) pure density, mid-window hump at u = 0.65, n = {n}")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(x)}   (rate curve peaks at {max(p_hat):.4f})")
    print(f"      detrended rho over lags 1..20: "
          f"[{min(prof):+.4f}, {max(prof):+.4f}]")
    print(f"      max |rho| = {max(abs(v) for v in prof):.4f}   "
          f"vs bar 0.05  ->  {'NULL' if max(abs(v) for v in prof) < 0.05 else 'DETECT'}")
    argmax = max(range(20), key=lambda i: abs(prof[i])) + 1
    print(f"      argmax lag = {argmax}   (no preferred lag: no shape)")

    # (b) injected lag-1 dependence: the power control
    lam = 0.35
    a_par = 0.5 * (1 - lam)
    b_par = 0.5 * (1 - lam)
    y = simulate_scan_markov(a_par, b_par, n, rng)
    p_flat = [sum(y) / n] * n
    profy = detrended_profile(y, p_flat, 20)
    argmaxy = max(range(20), key=lambda i: abs(profy[i])) + 1
    print(f"\n  (b) injected Markov dependence, lambda = {lam}")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(y)}")
    print(f"      detrended rho over lags 1..20: "
          f"[{min(profy):+.4f}, {max(profy):+.4f}]")
    print(f"      rho(1) = {profy[0]:+.4f}   theory lambda = {lam:+.4f}")
    print(f"      argmax lag = {argmaxy}   ->  "
          f"{'DETECTED at lag 1' if argmaxy == 1 else 'shape mismatch'}")
    print(f"      rho(2) = {profy[1]:+.4f}   theory lambda^2 = {lam**2:+.4f}"
          f"   (geometric decay)")

    # (c) coincidence scan: one spike then nothing
    latent = simulate_scan_density(lambda u: 0.6, n, rng)
    z = [latent[i] * latent[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1)]
    mu = sum(z) / len(z)
    profz = detrended_profile(z, [mu] * len(z), 6)
    print(f"\n  (c) coincidence scan Y_i = X_i X_{{i+1}}, latent q = 0.6")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(z)}   marginal rate = {mu:.4f} (theory 0.36)")
    print(f"      rho(1) = {profz[0]:+.4f}   theory q/(1+q) = {0.6/1.6:+.4f}")
    print(f"      rho(2..6) = {[round(v, 4) for v in profz[1:]]}   (theory: all 0)")
    print()
    print("  Verdict reproduced: density is null, dependence is caught, and the")
    print("  three mechanisms are told apart by the SHAPE of the first two lags.")
    print()

demos.description: An eight-part self-contained programme that reproduces every quantitative claim of the paper. Part 1 evaluates the mean-centring identity on five wildly different length-101 records -- iid Bernoulli, a smooth-hump Bernoulli, a strongly clustered block record, a non-binary deterministic ramp, and a single adversarial spike -- and finds the average autocorrelation equal to -0.01 in every case, to machine precision, confirming that a uniform negative offset is arithmetic rather than evidence. Part 2 computes lag profiles of the Fano, Singer and biplane cyclic difference sets, checks the identity C(k) = d_S(k) - |S|^2/n term by term, and shows that exact flatness occurs precisely at the level -1/(n-1) for these fully deterministic records while a non-difference set is far from flat. Part 3 evaluates the product Bernoulli expectation by exhaustive enumeration of all 2^12 configurations of a deliberately non-smooth rate curve and finds the true-curve-detrended statistic exactly zero at every lag, while the global-mean reading is not; it then checks the second-order curvature bound delta^2/v = 0.0101 against the 0.05 bar. Part 4 verifies the exact variance formula against enumeration and tabulates the 1/(16 m t^2) noise floor, reaching 0.0026 at the experiment's 9594 hits. Part 5 recovers the geometric Markov profile lambda^k by iterating the affine one-step map rather than the formula. Part 6 confirms the closed-form spike c(1-b)/(1-ab), the exact zeros beyond lag 1, the sharpness of the window bound against random search, and the approach of the supremum to 1. Part 7 runs the two-lag shape classifier on all three mechanisms plus the measured record. Part 8 is a Monte-Carlo replay at the experiment's scale: a density scan with a mid-window hump at u = 0.65 reads null, an injected Markov dependence is caught at lag 1 with geometric decay, and a coincidence scan produces one spike then nothing.
demos.code:
"""
Density versus Dependence in a Binary Scan
==========================================

Numerical demonstrations of the exact results on hit-indicator lag profiles.

The programme:

  1. The mean-centring identity.  For ANY cyclic record of length n, the average
     sample autocorrelation over the n-1 nonzero lags is exactly -1/(n-1).

  2. Difference sets realise the flat profile.  For a 0/1 record with support S,
     C(k) = d_S(k) - |S|^2/n; flat over nonzero lags iff S is a cyclic
     difference set, and the level is then exactly -1/(n-1).

  3. Pure density is exactly null when detrended at the true rate curve, and the
     literal global-mean reading is bounded by delta^2 / v uniformly in the lag.

  4. The Markov alternative has profile exactly lambda^k, peaking at lag 1.

  5. The coincidence (MA-1) scan has covariance p_i p_{i+1} p_{i+2} (1-p_{i+1})
     at lag 1 and EXACTLY zero at every lag >= 2, for every rate curve; its
     lag-1 correlation is c(1-b)/(1-ab), maximised over [l,u] by
     u(1-l)/(1-u l), attained by the alternating curve, with supremum 1.

  6. The noise floor 1/(16 m t^2), and the three-way shape classifier.

Self-contained: standard library plus (optional) numpy is NOT required.
Run with:  python3 demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from itertools import product
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 0.  Elementary helpers
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cyclic_autocov(x: Sequence[float], k: int) -> float:
    """Mean-centred cyclic autocovariance C(k) = sum_i r_i r_{i+k}, r = x - mean."""
    n = len(x)
    mean = sum(x) / n
    r = [xi - mean for xi in x]
    return sum(r[i] * r[(i + k) % n] for i in range(n))


def cyclic_autocorr_profile(x: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """rho(k) = C(k)/C(0) for k = 1 .. n-1."""
    n = len(x)
    c0 = cyclic_autocov(x, 0)
    if c0 == 0.0:
        raise ValueError("constant record: autocorrelation undefined")
    return [cyclic_autocov(x, k) / c0 for k in range(1, n)]


def difference_multiplicity(support: Sequence[int], n: int, k: int) -> int:
    """d_S(k) = #{a in S : a + k mod n in S}."""
    s = set(a % n for a in support)
    return sum(1 for a in s if (a + k) % n in s)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 1.  The mean-centring identity:  average rho(k) = -1/(n-1)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_mean_centring_identity(seed: int = 599) -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("1.  THE MEAN-CENTRING IDENTITY:  mean of rho(k) over k != 0 is -1/(n-1)")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    cases: List[Tuple[str, List[float]]] = [
        ("iid Bernoulli(0.5), n=101",
         [float(rng.random() < 0.5) for _ in range(101)]),
        ("Bernoulli with a smooth hump, n=101",
         [float(rng.random() < 0.5 + 0.05 * math.sin(math.pi * i / 100))
          for i in range(101)]),
        ("strongly clustered record (blocks), n=101",
         [float((i // 7) % 2 == 0) for i in range(101)]),
        ("deterministic ramp (not 0/1 at all), n=101",
         [float(i) ** 1.3 for i in range(101)]),
        ("adversarial: one spike, n=101",
         [1.0 if i == 17 else 0.0 for i in range(101)]),
    ]

    print(f"{'record':<42}{'mean rho':>14}{'-1/(n-1)':>14}")
    print("-" * 70)
    for name, x in cases:
        prof = cyclic_autocorr_profile(x)
        m = sum(prof) / len(prof)
        n = len(x)
        print(f"{name:<42}{m:>14.10f}{-1.0/(n-1):>14.10f}")
    print()
    print("  The identity holds for random records, structured records, and")
    print("  non-binary records alike.  It is an algebraic property of centring,")
    print("  not a probabilistic statement.  A uniform ~ -0.01 offset on a")
    print("  101-position window is therefore FORCED, not evidence of inhibition.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 2.  Difference sets realise exact flatness at -1/(n-1)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_difference_sets() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("2.  EXACT FLATNESS  <=>  CYCLIC DIFFERENCE SET,  AT LEVEL -1/(n-1)")
    print("=" * 78)

    examples: List[Tuple[str, int, List[int]]] = [
        ("Fano plane      S = {0,1,3} in Z_7",   7,  [0, 1, 3]),
        ("Singer (13,4,1) S = {0,1,3,9} in Z_13", 13, [0, 1, 3, 9]),
        ("Biplane (11,5,2) S = {1,3,4,5,9} in Z_11", 11, [1, 3, 4, 5, 9]),
        ("NOT a difference set: {0,1,2} in Z_7", 7, [0, 1, 2]),
    ]

    for name, n, S in examples:
        x = [1.0 if i in S else 0.0 for i in range(n)]
        prof = cyclic_autocorr_profile(x)
        d = [difference_multiplicity(S, n, k) for k in range(1, n)]
        flat = max(prof) - min(prof) < 1e-12
        print(f"\n  {name}")
        print(f"    d_S(k), k=1..{n-1}      : {d}")
        print(f"    rho(k)                : {[round(v, 6) for v in prof]}")
        print(f"    difference mult const : {len(set(d)) == 1}")
        print(f"    profile flat          : {flat}")
        if flat:
            print(f"    level                 : {prof[0]:.10f}"
                  f"   (-1/(n-1) = {-1.0/(n-1):.10f})")
        # verify C(k) = d_S(k) - |S|^2/n
        errs = [abs(cyclic_autocov(x, k) - (d[k - 1] - len(S) ** 2 / n))
                for k in range(1, n)]
        print(f"    max |C(k) - (d_S(k) - |S|^2/n)| = {max(errs):.2e}")
    print()
    print("  The flattest possible 0/1 records are the most DETERMINISTIC ones.")
    print("  Flatness is a design-theoretic signature, not a randomness one.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 3.  Pure density: exact null, and the second-order curvature bound
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def exact_bernoulli_expectation(p: Sequence[float],
                                f: Callable[[Tuple[int, ...]], float]) -> float:
    """Exact expectation over all 2^n configurations of a product-Bernoulli law."""
    n = len(p)
    total = 0.0
    for s in product((0, 1), repeat=n):
        w = 1.0
        for i in range(n):
            w *= p[i] if s[i] else 1.0 - p[i]
        total += w * f(s)
    return total


def centered_pair_sum(s: Tuple[int, ...], k: int, m: int,
                      c: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    return sum((s[i] - c[i]) * (s[i + k] - c[i + k]) for i in range(m))


def demo_pure_density_exact_null() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("3.  PURE DENSITY:  EXACT NULL WHEN DETRENDED AT THE TRUE RATE CURVE")
    print("=" * 78)

    # A deliberately wild, non-smooth rate curve on n = 12 positions.
    n = 12
    p = [0.13, 0.91, 0.44, 0.07, 0.66, 0.50, 0.83, 0.22, 0.95, 0.31, 0.58, 0.72]
    print(f"  rate curve p (n={n}, arbitrary, non-smooth):")
    print(f"    {p}")
    print()
    print(f"  {'lag k':>6}{'E[A_k detrended at p]':>26}{'E[A_k at global mean]':>26}")
    print("  " + "-" * 56)
    gm = sum(p) / n
    for k in range(1, 6):
        m = n - k
        e_true = exact_bernoulli_expectation(
            p, lambda s, k=k, m=m: centered_pair_sum(s, k, m, p))
        e_lit = exact_bernoulli_expectation(
            p, lambda s, k=k, m=m: centered_pair_sum(s, k, m, [gm] * n))
        print(f"  {k:>6}{e_true:>26.15f}{e_lit:>26.10f}")
    print()
    print("  Detrending at the TRUE curve is exactly zero at every lag, to machine")
    print("  precision, for a curve with no smoothness whatsoever.  The literal")
    print("  global-mean reading is not zero -- that residue is curvature.")
    print()

    # Curvature bound: |E[A_k]/(m v)| <= delta^2 / v.
    print("  Curvature bound  |rho_literal| <= delta^2 / v  (uniform in the lag):")
    delta, v = 0.05, 0.45 * 0.55
    n2 = 14
    q = [0.5 + delta * math.sin(2 * math.pi * i / n2) for i in range(n2)]
    gm2 = sum(q) / n2
    worst = 0.0
    for k in range(1, 8):
        m = n2 - k
        e = sum((q[i] - gm2) * (q[i + k] - gm2) for i in range(m))
        worst = max(worst, abs(e / (m * v)))
    print(f"    delta = {delta}, v = {v:.6f},  bound delta^2/v = {delta**2/v:.6f}")
    print(f"    worst observed |rho| over lags 1..7 = {worst:.6f}")
    print(f"    bar = 0.05   ->  curvature cannot fake H1: "
          f"{delta**2/v < 0.05}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 4.  Variance, and the noise floor 1/(16 m t^2)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_variance_and_noise_floor() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("4.  EXACT VARIANCE  sum_i p_i(1-p_i) p_{i+k}(1-p_{i+k})  AND NOISE FLOOR")
    print("=" * 78)

    n = 12
    p = [0.13, 0.91, 0.44, 0.07, 0.66, 0.50, 0.83, 0.22, 0.95, 0.31, 0.58, 0.72]
    print(f"  {'lag k':>6}{'exact E[A_k^2]':>22}{'sum V_i V_{i+k}':>22}")
    print("  " + "-" * 50)
    for k in range(1, 5):
        m = n - k
        lhs = exact_bernoulli_expectation(
            p, lambda s, k=k, m=m: centered_pair_sum(s, k, m, p) ** 2)
        rhs = sum(p[i] * (1 - p[i]) * p[i + k] * (1 - p[i + k]) for i in range(m))
        print(f"  {k:>6}{lhs:>22.12f}{rhs:>22.12f}")
    print()
    print("  The terms are pairwise uncorrelated EVEN WHEN TWO PAIRS SHARE A")
    print("  POSITION (j = i+k), which is why the variance is a clean sum.")
    print()

    print("  Chebyshev noise floor  P[|A_k| >= t m] <= 1/(16 m t^2):")
    for m, t in [(100, 0.05), (1000, 0.05), (9594, 0.05), (9594, 0.02)]:
        print(f"    m = {m:>6}, t = {t:<5} ->  bound = {1.0/(16*m*t*t):.6f}")
    print()
    print("  At the experiment's m = 9594 hits and the 0.05 bar the bound is")
    print(f"  {1.0/(16*9594*0.05**2):.6f} < 0.003: the null is an EXCLUSION, not a shrug.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 5.  The Markov alternative: profile exactly lambda^k
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def markov_profile(a: float, b: float, kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    """rho(k) computed by iterating the affine one-step map, not by the formula."""
    lam = 1.0 - a - b
    pi = a / (a + b)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        x = 1.0
        for _ in range(k):
            x = x * (1 - b) + (1 - x) * a
        cov = pi * (x - pi)
        out.append(cov / (pi * (1 - pi)))
    return out


def demo_markov_profile() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("5.  MARKOV ALTERNATIVE:  rho(k) = lambda^k EXACTLY, PEAKING AT LAG 1")
    print("=" * 78)
    for a, b in [(0.2, 0.3), (0.05, 0.05), (0.6, 0.1), (0.4, 0.6)]:
        lam = 1 - a - b
        prof = markov_profile(a, b, 6)
        pred = [lam ** k for k in range(1, 7)]
        err = max(abs(x - y) for x, y in zip(prof, pred))
        argmax = max(range(6), key=lambda i: abs(prof[i])) + 1
        print(f"\n  a = {a}, b = {b}   lambda = {lam:+.3f}   "
              f"stationary rate = {a/(a+b):.4f}")
        print(f"    iterated profile : {[round(v, 8) for v in prof]}")
        print(f"    lambda^k         : {[round(v, 8) for v in pred]}")
        print(f"    max deviation    : {err:.2e}     argmax lag = {argmax}")
    print()
    print("  lambda = 0 (a + b = 1) gives the memoryless chain and a profile that")
    print("  vanishes identically: memory and lag-1 correlation are the SAME thing.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 6.  The coincidence (MA-1) scan
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def ma_profile_exact(p: Sequence[float], i: int, kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    """Lag profile of Y_j = X_j X_{j+1} anchored at i, by exact enumeration."""
    n = len(p)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        if i + k + 1 >= n:
            break
        mu_i = p[i] * p[i + 1]
        mu_ik = p[i + k] * p[i + k + 1]
        cov = exact_bernoulli_expectation(
            p, lambda s, i=i, k=k, mu_i=mu_i, mu_ik=mu_ik:
            (s[i] * s[i + 1] - mu_i) * (s[i + k] * s[i + k + 1] - mu_ik))
        var = mu_i - mu_i ** 2
        out.append(cov / var)
    return out


def spike_bound(l: float, u: float) -> float:
    """Sigma(l,u) = u(1-l)/(1-ul): the sharp maximum coincidence spike."""
    return u * (1 - l) / (1 - u * l)


def alt_rate(l: float, u: float, n: int) -> List[float]:
    """The alternating rate curve u, l, u, l, ... which attains the bound."""
    return [l if j % 2 == 1 else u for j in range(n)]


def demo_coincidence_scan() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6.  THE COINCIDENCE (MA-1) SCAN:  ONE SPIKE, THEN EXACT ZEROS")
    print("=" * 78)

    n = 11
    curves: List[Tuple[str, List[float]]] = [
        ("constant q = 0.5", [0.5] * n),
        ("constant q = 0.8", [0.8] * n),
        ("wild heterogeneous", [0.2, 0.9, 0.35, 0.75, 0.1, 0.6, 0.45,
                                0.85, 0.3, 0.55, 0.7]),
        ("alternating 0.9/0.1", alt_rate(0.1, 0.9, n)),
    ]
    for name, p in curves:
        prof = ma_profile_exact(p, 0, 5)
        a, b, c = p[0], p[1], p[2]
        closed = c * (1 - b) / (1 - a * b)
        print(f"\n  {name}")
        print(f"    exact profile rho_Y(k), k=1..{len(prof)}:")
        print(f"      {[round(v, 12) for v in prof]}")
        print(f"    closed form c(1-b)/(1-ab) = {closed:.12f}"
              f"   (lag-1 match: {abs(prof[0]-closed) < 1e-12})")
        print(f"    max |rho_Y(k)| for k >= 2 : {max((abs(v) for v in prof[1:]), default=0.0):.2e}")
    print()
    print("  EXACT zeros from lag 2 on, for EVERY rate curve.  A Markov profile")
    print("  lambda^k can never do this without also vanishing at lag 1.")
    print()

    print("  Sharpness of the window bound Sigma(l,u) = u(1-l)/(1-ul):")
    print(f"  {'[l, u]':>16}{'Sigma(l,u)':>14}{'alt-curve spike':>18}"
          f"{'random-curve max':>20}")
    print("  " + "-" * 68)
    rng = random.Random(2026)
    for l, u in [(0.1, 0.9), (0.3, 0.7), (0.45, 0.55), (0.01, 0.99)]:
        sigma = spike_bound(l, u)
        p_alt = alt_rate(l, u, 5)
        attained = p_alt[2] * (1 - p_alt[1]) / (1 - p_alt[0] * p_alt[1])
        best = 0.0
        for _ in range(20000):
            a = rng.uniform(l, u); b = rng.uniform(l, u); c = rng.uniform(l, u)
            best = max(best, c * (1 - b) / (1 - a * b))
        print(f"  [{l:.2f}, {u:.2f}]".rjust(16)
              + f"{sigma:>14.8f}{attained:>18.8f}{best:>20.8f}")
    print()
    print("  Random search never exceeds Sigma, and the alternating curve hits it")
    print("  exactly.  So Sigma is the MAXIMUM, not merely an upper bound.")
    print()

    print("  Heterogeneity beats the homogeneous cap q/(1+q) < 1/2:")
    print(f"    constant q = 0.99 : spike = {0.99/1.99:.6f}  (< 0.5 always)")
    print(f"    alternating 0.1/0.9: spike = {spike_bound(0.1, 0.9):.6f} = 81/91")
    print()
    print("  Supremum over all curves with values in (0,1) is exactly 1:")
    print(f"    {'t':>10}{'Sigma(t, 1-t)':>18}")
    for t in [0.25, 0.1, 0.01, 1e-3, 1e-5]:
        print(f"    {t:>10}{spike_bound(t, 1 - t):>18.10f}")
    print()
    print("  ...but never reaches 1.  AMPLITUDE CARRIES NO MECHANISM INFORMATION;")
    print("  only SHAPE (exact zeros from lag 2) does.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 7.  The three-way shape classifier
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def classify_profile(rho1: float, rho2: float, tol: float = 0.01) -> str:
    """Classify a mechanism from the first two lags alone (Trichotomy theorem)."""
    if abs(rho1) <= tol and abs(rho2) <= tol:
        return "pure density (flat)"
    if abs(rho1) > tol and abs(rho2) <= tol:
        return "coincidence / MA-1 (one spike)"
    if abs(rho2 - rho1 ** 2) <= tol:
        return f"Markov (geometric, lambda ~ {rho1:+.3f})"
    return "unclassified"


def demo_shape_classifier() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("7.  THE THREE-WAY SHAPE CLASSIFIER (FIRST TWO LAGS SUFFICE)")
    print("=" * 78)

    n = 9
    samples: List[Tuple[str, float, float]] = []

    # pure density: exactly zero
    samples.append(("pure density, arbitrary curve", 0.0, 0.0))

    # Markov chains
    for a, b in [(0.2, 0.3), (0.6, 0.1)]:
        prof = markov_profile(a, b, 2)
        samples.append((f"Markov a={a}, b={b}", prof[0], prof[1]))

    # coincidence scans
    for name, p in [("coincidence, q = 0.6", [0.6] * n),
                    ("coincidence, alternating 0.1/0.9", alt_rate(0.1, 0.9, n))]:
        prof = ma_profile_exact(p, 0, 2)
        samples.append((name, prof[0], prof[1]))

    # the measured record
    samples.append(("MEASURED RECORD (lags 1,2)", -0.0199, -0.0104))

    print(f"  {'mechanism':<36}{'rho(1)':>10}{'rho(2)':>10}   verdict")
    print("  " + "-" * 84)
    for name, r1, r2 in samples:
        print(f"  {name:<36}{r1:>10.4f}{r2:>10.4f}   {classify_profile(r1, r2, 0.03)}")
    print()
    print("  Note the measured record: both lags sit at the arithmetic artefact")
    print("  level, far below the 0.05 bar.  Density, and nothing else.")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 8.  A Monte-Carlo replay of the experimental verdict
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def simulate_scan_density(rate: Callable[[float], float], n: int,
                          rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    return [1 if rng.random() < rate(i / (n - 1)) else 0 for i in range(n)]


def simulate_scan_markov(a: float, b: float, n: int,
                         rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    pi = a / (a + b)
    x = 1 if rng.random() < pi else 0
    out = [x]
    for _ in range(n - 1):
        x = (1 if rng.random() >= b else 0) if x == 1 else (1 if rng.random() < a else 0)
        out.append(x)
    return out


def detrended_profile(x: Sequence[int], p_hat: Sequence[float],
                      kmax: int) -> List[float]:
    n = len(x)
    denom = sum(ph * (1 - ph) for ph in p_hat)
    out = []
    for k in range(1, kmax + 1):
        m = n - k
        num = sum((x[i] - p_hat[i]) * (x[i + k] - p_hat[i + k]) for i in range(m))
        scale = sum(p_hat[i] * (1 - p_hat[i]) for i in range(m))
        out.append(num / scale if scale else 0.0)
    return out


def demo_monte_carlo_replay(seed: int = 599) -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("8.  MONTE-CARLO REPLAY:  DENSITY IS NULL, INJECTED DEPENDENCE IS CAUGHT")
    print("=" * 78)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    n = 9594

    # (a) pure density with a mid-window hump at u ~ 0.65
    def rate(u: float) -> float:
        return 0.50 + 0.05 * math.exp(-((u - 0.65) ** 2) / (2 * 0.08 ** 2))

    x = simulate_scan_density(rate, n, rng)
    p_hat = [rate(i / (n - 1)) for i in range(n)]
    prof = detrended_profile(x, p_hat, 20)
    print(f"\n  (a) pure density, mid-window hump at u = 0.65, n = {n}")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(x)}   (rate curve peaks at {max(p_hat):.4f})")
    print(f"      detrended rho over lags 1..20: "
          f"[{min(prof):+.4f}, {max(prof):+.4f}]")
    print(f"      max |rho| = {max(abs(v) for v in prof):.4f}   "
          f"vs bar 0.05  ->  {'NULL' if max(abs(v) for v in prof) < 0.05 else 'DETECT'}")
    argmax = max(range(20), key=lambda i: abs(prof[i])) + 1
    print(f"      argmax lag = {argmax}   (no preferred lag: no shape)")

    # (b) injected lag-1 dependence: the power control
    lam = 0.35
    a_par = 0.5 * (1 - lam)
    b_par = 0.5 * (1 - lam)
    y = simulate_scan_markov(a_par, b_par, n, rng)
    p_flat = [sum(y) / n] * n
    profy = detrended_profile(y, p_flat, 20)
    argmaxy = max(range(20), key=lambda i: abs(profy[i])) + 1
    print(f"\n  (b) injected Markov dependence, lambda = {lam}")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(y)}")
    print(f"      detrended rho over lags 1..20: "
          f"[{min(profy):+.4f}, {max(profy):+.4f}]")
    print(f"      rho(1) = {profy[0]:+.4f}   theory lambda = {lam:+.4f}")
    print(f"      argmax lag = {argmaxy}   ->  "
          f"{'DETECTED at lag 1' if argmaxy == 1 else 'shape mismatch'}")
    print(f"      rho(2) = {profy[1]:+.4f}   theory lambda^2 = {lam**2:+.4f}"
          f"   (geometric decay)")

    # (c) coincidence scan: one spike then nothing
    latent = simulate_scan_density(lambda u: 0.6, n, rng)
    z = [latent[i] * latent[i + 1] for i in range(n - 1)]
    mu = sum(z) / len(z)
    profz = detrended_profile(z, [mu] * len(z), 6)
    print(f"\n  (c) coincidence scan Y_i = X_i X_{{i+1}}, latent q = 0.6")
    print(f"      hits = {sum(z)}   marginal rate = {mu:.4f} (theory 0.36)")
    print(f"      rho(1) = {profz[0]:+.4f}   theory q/(1+q) = {0.6/1.6:+.4f}")
    print(f"      rho(2..6) = {[round(v, 4) for v in profz[1:]]}   (theory: all 0)")

    print("  Verdict reproduced: density is null, dependence is caught, and the")
    print("  three mechanisms are told apart by the SHAPE of the first two lags.")

def main() -> None:
